card.band: 8h. Correctness is quick (the stored-block path), while ratio needs real entropy modeling. A frontier agent reaches a basic LZ77+Huffman encoder but averages below the reference ratio. A weaker model stays on uncompressed output.
card.cheat: Emitting stored blocks gives round-trip validity but only minimal credit. The decoder is a binary and no encoder is shipped.
card.grading: Every output is decoded by the sealed reference decoder and must round-trip exactly on hidden mixed corpora (text, binary, tiny, empty, large). Credit scales with the compressed-size ratio against the reference encoder at each quality, per bucket. Invalid streams score 0 for the file.
card.reference: The upstream C encoder gives the ceiling for ratio. A reference built by us from the spec targets about 85% of its size efficiency, in roughly 3k lines.
card.source: https://github.com/google/brotli @ v1.2.0, MIT. Testdata corpora licences are unverified, so the bundle uses its own generated and public-domain inputs.
card.task: /app ships the RFC 7932 text, the static dictionary and a reference decoder binary. The agent writes a Brotli compressor in Rust with qualities 0-9, window sizes, metablock splitting, context modeling and dictionary references. The CLI reads stdin and writes stdout.
card.title: Brotli encoder with decoder-verified quality levels

v1.kill_reason: A permissive Rust port (dropbox rust-brotli, BSD-3/MIT, v9.0.0) is a direct no-stdlib port of the C encoder, bitwise identical at levels 0-9. That matches the deliverable exactly, so a frontier agent can recall or reconstruct the approach and the task is too easy. The seed's own note says the project was already dropped as too easy. Also, brotli is on the CROWDED list (Nov 1), and the three source SHAs (38e5ee3, 7b93874, 028fb5a) are unreconciled.

Band.why: No dated evidence; a bitwise-identical Rust port is public, so frontier agents may recall the approach and the band is more likely too easy than in range.

Build.why: Writing a 3k-line reference plus the differential harness is about 3 days.

Fit.why: CPU-only Rust encoder and C reference fit the sandbox; the 8-core build is cheap.

Hor.why: A roughly 3k-line encoder with entropy modeling and metablock splitting fits the 8h tier.

Lic.why: MIT for upstream and BSD-3/MIT for the Rust port; both allow shipping.

Multi.why: Qualities, window sizes, corpora buckets and dictionary references give several independent partial-credit levers.

Nov.why: Brotli is on the CROWDED codec list, the same subject as the l0 neighbour, and a public Rust port matches the deliverable.

Real.why: Real google/brotli v1.2.0 with MIT LICENSE and RFC 7932; SHA mismatch noted but the repo is real.

Ref.why: Upstream C encoder is a complete permissive implementation and would score about 1.

Seal.why: The C encoder and the Rust port are public and not shipped; the agent can recall the outline, which is a difficulty question under K8, not sealing.

Surf.why: Differential fuzz through the reference decoder gives unlimited cases with per-quality ratio buckets.

spike_plan.kill_if: Outputs differ materially in size; then the lookup is partial and the idea is re-scored Band and Nov, not killed on K8.
spike_plan.pass_if: Rust port output differs from C output at none of the tested qualities, which would confirm the direct lookup and kill the idea.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, clone dropbox/rust-brotli and build its compressor at quality 0-9 (cargo build --release).
Clone google/brotli at v1.2.0 and build the C encoder (cmake, already green in smoke_build).
Compress a mixed corpus (text, binary, tiny, empty, 10 MB) with both encoders at qualities 0,5,9 and compare output bytes with cmp.
If the outputs are byte-identical, record the lookup as direct (already a public Rust port matching the deliverable).
Also decode the Rust output with the C decoder to confirm the round-trip, then stop.

v1.summary: Brotli is a real, MIT-licensed, sealed-decoder subject with a strong, unverified-band reference, but a public Rust port matches the deliverable bitwise at levels 0-9, so lookup is direct. Killed K8 (too easy, famous port exists); the seed's own source notes already flag it as dropped for this reason.
